convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to call the external Bezier custom indicator (Bezier.mq5) which implements a Bernstein polynomial smoothing algorithm with custom price types and sensitivity coefficient. The scale-in (ReOpen/dolivka) logic with position comment parsing for tracking add-on trades adds complexity beyond simple entry/exit. External .mqh library (TradeAlgorithms.mqh) handles all trade execution, position sizing, and time-level guards.

other_exits: Opposite signal closes position: BUY_Close triggered when Bezier[SignalBar+1]>Bezier[SignalBar+2] (downtrend detected), SELL_Close triggered when Bezier[SignalBar+1]<Bezier[SignalBar+2] (uptrend detected)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: If MM<0: fixed lot = abs(MM). If MM>=0 with MMMode=FREEMARGIN: lot = FreeMargin*MM. If BALANCE: lot = Balance*MM. If LOSSFREEMARGIN: lot sized so max loss = FreeMargin*MM based on SL. If LOSSBALANCE: lot sized so max loss = Balance*MM based on SL. If LOT: fixed lot = abs(MM). Default MMMode=LOT so default is fixed lot = abs(MM) = 0.1. Scale-in (ReOpen) trades always use LOT mode regardless of MMMode setting.

custom_logic_notes: Scale-in (dolivka/ReOpen) system: After initial entry, if price moves favorably by PriceStep pips (default 300), additional positions are added up to PosTotal (default 10) times. The position comment string encodes the add-on count, last entry price, and lot size for tracking. When an existing position is detected (PositionSelect), the EA parses the comment to get OrderTotal, OpenPrice, and LastLot. If OrderTotal < PosTotal and price distance from last entry > PriceStep, a scale-in signal is generated. Scale-in trades use BuyLotCount with LOT mode (fixed lot = abs(MM)) regardless of the MMMode setting. The Bezier indicator uses a Bernstein polynomial (Bezier curve) smoothing with factorial-based binomial coefficients and a sensitivity parameter T (0 to 1). Signal logic: Value[1]<Value[2] means Bezier is rising (uptrend) - triggers BUY_Open if Value[0]>Value[1] (current bar above previous = direction change upward). Value[1]>Value[2] means Bezier is falling (downtrend) - triggers SELL_Open if Value[0]<Value[1]. Time-level guard prevents re-entry until next bar time is reached after a trade (stored as GlobalVariable). The EA supports multi-timeframe operation: indicator timeframe (InpInd_Timeframe) can differ from chart timeframe, with new-bar detection on the indicator timeframe. SignalBar=0 allows intrabar recalculation, SignalBar>=1 requires new bar.
python_conversion_notes: The Bezier custom indicator must be reimplemented in Python - it uses Bernstein polynomial basis: B(n,k,t) = C(n,k)*t^k*(1-t)^(n-k) applied to price series. The custom price types (PRICE_SIMPL, PRICE_QUARTER, PRICE_TRENDFOLLOW0/1, PRICE_DEMARK) need to be implemented. The scale-in (ReOpen) logic tracks add-on trade state via MT5 position comments - in Python this should be tracked via a separate state manager or database since Python backtest frameworks don't have position comments. The multi-timeframe support (indicator on H4, chart can be different) requires proper bar alignment and resampling. Position sizing has 5 modes including loss-based sizing that requires margin calculation - need to implement OrderCalcProfit equivalent or use broker margin data. The TimeLevel guard using GlobalVariables must be replaced with in-memory state tracking. StopLoss/TakeProfit values in the EA are in points (not pips), so no digit adjustment is needed - they are multiplied directly by SymbolInfoDouble(SYMBOL_POINT).
